chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: May I be made your ransom, I perform ghusl in the privy in which urine is passed, while wearing Sindī sandals,
So he said: “If the water that flows from your body reaches the bottom of your feet, then do not wash your feet.”

key_terms.أَغْتَسِلُ: I perform ghusl, meaning ritual washing of the body
key_terms.فَلَا تَغْسِلْ قَدَمَيْكَ: then do not wash your feet
key_terms.نَعْلٍ سِنْدِيَّةٍ: Sindī sandals worn on the feet

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to wash their feet separately after ghusl if water from the body has already reached them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl in a place where urine is passed and the effect of flowing water on the feet. It indicates that if the water running from the body reaches the underside of the feet during ghusl, there is no need to wash the feet separately.
